canon.name: the Samaritan
canon.text: the Samaritan: adult man of middle age, sturdy and weathered build, olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-cropped beard, plain lined face with steady eyes. Signature outfit worn on the road: undyed linen tunic in earth tones of ochre and brown with a dusty woollen cloak in deep blue-grey, sandals and a leather belt bearing a small pouch of coins. Carries alone a water skin and a folded cloth for binding wounds.

canon.name: Wounded traveler in the Samaritan parable
canon.text: Wounded traveler: a man of about 30 to 45 years, of average build with a lean, weathered frame, olive skin, short dark hair and a close-cut beard. Facial features are plain and worn, marked with dust and bruising. Stripped to a simple loincloth of undyed linen, he has no cloak or sandals. Signature props: none.

canon.name: Jerusalem–Jericho road in the Samaritan parable
canon.text: Jerusalem–Jericho road: a steep, stony track descending through the arid Judean wilderness from the hill city toward the low Jordan valley. Rocky limestone ridges and gullies line the way, with dry scrub, scattered acacia and thorn, and patches of wild grass. Rough boulders and cairns mark the path, and distant terraced hills and the faint outline of a walled town lie ahead in the desert haze.
